races.name: Juddmonte 'Lead Artist' Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden
Hailey Equine Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Al Shira'aa Racing Meadow Court Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Dreamasar
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with strong recent form (three wins from five runs including back-to-back victories), handles Good ground well, Billy Loughnane rides, and the step up to 1m2f from 1m has already been successfully negotiated — second only in class to the top-rated runners here, making the prominent pitch ideal.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last five starts show ability, though fourth last time was more workmanlike. Has raced over today's trip and going before, and a 22-day break keeps her fresh — capable of a bold showing without quite matching the leading pair here.

runners_data.name: Francophone
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator for Oisin Murphy, but recent form reads poorly (6-1-4-0-0) and all five recent runs have been at shorter trips on Good ground where he has not threatened; needs a much faster pace collapse than this race shape is likely to produce.
runners_data.comment: A mare with a win four starts back and rated third of eight on our figures, backed by a strong speed figure. Already has today's trip and going under her belt, though back-to-back unplaced efforts in her last two starts are the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Moody
runners_data.note: In excellent heart with back-to-back wins including a Listed success at 1m4f on Good, but a natural front-end or close-tracking type who will be pushed into a midfield berth here by the crowded prominent positions — tongue-tie fitted, and the positional compromise means his finishing kick may arrive too late despite his talent.
runners_data.comment: Really progressive filly, winner of her last three starts for a near-perfect recent record. A 74-day absence since that latest success is the obvious concern fitness-wise, but the underlying form makes her a serious threat regardless.

runners_data.name: Nyra
runners_data.note: Consistent, prominent-style performer for Dylan Browne McMonagle and Joseph O'Brien (20 winners from 56 in 14 days), with five consecutive top-four finishes at 1m2f-1m4f on similar ground — the horse who sits second or third to One Look and quickens is this filly's blueprint.
runners_data.comment: Ultra-consistent filly, placed in four of her last five starts and runner-up again last time out. Rated second of eight here, but remains without a win in that sequence and needs to find more to break through.

runners_data.name: One Look
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for James Doyle and P. Twomey, highest-rated runner in the field (OR 111) with headgear worn, and has hit the frame in 9 of 15 runs on Good ground; racing slightly out of natural role given its OR suggests it should face stronger company, but uncontested lead access makes this a strong tactical position.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated on our figures with a strong speed figure to match, this mare was runner-up last time out and also five starts back. She already has today's trip and going under her belt - the one knock is she's yet to get her head in front recently.

runners_data.name: Rhapsody
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer for Ryan Moore (William Haggas yard), but squeezed out of its preferred position by the volume of forward types; recent form is mixed (4-3-1-5-8) and the step back to 1m2f from shorter trips leaves trip confidence moderate — positional disadvantage is the dominant concern.
runners_data.comment: Rhapsody won three starts back and has since finished third and fourth, a gentle fade from that peak. Already has today's trip and going under her belt, and a moderate speed figure fits a midfield finish rather than a leading role.

runners_data.name: Spicy Margarita
runners_data.note: True hold-up type for Donagh O'Connor, redistibuted to midfield on the map, with a trainer showing zero winners from 14 in the past fortnight; recent form (5-0-5-8-4) is uninspiring and there is no evidence of the pace collapse needed to bring her into play on Good to Firm ground.
runners_data.comment: Spicy Margarita has missed the frame in each of her last five starts and sits second-bottom of our rankings. She has run over today's trip before and a quick 20-day turnaround keeps her fresh, but she remains without a win and hard to trust on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Subsonic
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with headgear (hood and tongue-tie), won over 1m2f on Soft but recent Good-ground form disappoints (6th, 7th, 8th) and the step back to 1m2f from longer trips is untested at this level — Ben Coen rides but needs an unlikely tempo surge to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Subsonic sits bottom of our rankings and was well beaten last time out, though a win three starts back shows latent ability. She has run over today's trip before, but a modest speed figure leaves plenty to find here.

races.paceDynamic: One Look is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m2f on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh. Dreamasar and Nyra will track close behind in the prominent positions, creating an organised, single-file shape with a measured tempo that suits those who can quicken off a true pace rather than grind rivals into submission. The field actually contains more prominent-natured horses than can occupy those forward positions: Moody and Rhapsody are natural front-end types who will find themselves shuffled into midfield roles they do not naturally fill, diluting their effectiveness. This controlled, front-led shape with a compressed mid-race tempo heavily favours prominent racers who can accelerate off a true pace — and those tracking One Look in second and third are best positioned to exploit the final-furlong kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If One Look dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the race is decided by a turn-of-foot in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: One Look sets fractions that suit those tracking within two lengths, and the horse with the best late acceleration from a prominent pitch wins as the field arrives together at the two-pole; Good to Firm ground rewards that sharp, upward gear-change rather than relentless galloping ability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If One Look's uncontested pace is slow enough to conserve energy, and no prominent tracker produces a clean enough challenge to close the gap.
scenarios.body: One Look, unchallenged and comfortable on Good to Firm ground with headgear, simply never comes off the bridle until late and outstays challengers whose kicks arrive too late over this 1m2f trip; this is more plausible if Nyra and Dreamasar overcommit chasing early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is faster than anticipated and the leaders come back to the field in the final furlong, opening the door for those ridden off the pace.
scenarios.body: Francophone and Subsonic, genuinely held up, would be the primary beneficiaries if the prominent bunch overcook the early fractions and the race turns into a stamina test rather than a speed exercise; however, neither has shown consistent form on Good to Firm ground at this level, limiting confidence in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types — Moody and Rhapsody — fight for position mid-race, creating a ragged, uneven tempo that scrambles the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: A fractured gallop with horses racing out of their natural roles could produce a rough, unpredictable finish where the winner emerges from a bunched group late; Moody, if finding a rhythm despite the positional compromise, would be the chief beneficiary given recent winning form, though the low STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence materially.

watchPoints.text: One Look's ability to control tempo entirely unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if James Doyle allows even a fraction too slow a pace, the prominent trackers Nyra and Dreamasar may simply glide past without a genuine test.

Moody and Rhapsody are both natural front-end types who cannot get their preferred positions here — watch for traffic issues or positional friction in the first two furlongs as they attempt to find their rhythm from an unnatural midfield berth.

Francophone has been in poor form for five consecutive runs and is expected to race from the rear; if the pace is honest, Ryan Moore's use of Rhapsody from midfield could block the run-through channels that Francophone and Subsonic need late.

Good to Firm conditions at the Curragh have been consistent all day — no runner has a ground concern, but horses who have won on softer surfaces (Moody, Subsonic) should be monitored for whether the quicker ground blunts their finishing effort.
Spicy Margarita's trainer has zero winners from 14 runners in the past 14 days — a cold statistical flag worth tracking, particularly given the filly's already-uninspiring recent form profile.

races.name: Liverpool FC Foundation Scurry Handicap

runners_data.name: Keke
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner; W J Lee and Lynam in sharp form (1/4 in 14 days), five wins recorded on good ground, but steps up from 5-6f and the 6½f trip on this track is an open question — if he handles it, he controls the race.
runners_data.comment: Keke won last time out, and was also successful four starts back, landing two of his last five starts. He has run over today's trip and going before and returns fresh on a 14-day break, though the moderate efforts sandwiched in between are the one blemish on a strong profile.

runners_data.name: Bodhi Bear
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partnership is significant at the Curragh; both turf wins came on good ground and he handles 6f comfortably, making this trip a small extension — prominent style suits the anticipated race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Bodhi Bear won two starts back and again five starts back, but was only beaten into third last time out, landing two of his last five races. He has run over today's trip and going before, returns fresh on a 20-day break, and carries the leading rating in this field — that below-par latest effort is the one blot.

runners_data.name: Tango Flare
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran with exceptional course-and-distance form (14/15 runs on similar going, two wins), wears a hood; genuine hold-up type who benefits if the prominent cluster pushes the gallop beyond sustainable levels.
runners_data.comment: Tango Flare followed a blank run with a win two starts back and second last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before and is fresh on a 20-day break, with that earlier below-par effort the only blemish on an improving profile.

runners_data.name: The Highway Rat
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up specialist wearing a visor; recent run just six days ago is worth monitoring for freshness, and his best going figures come on good ground — needs pace to collapse to land a blow from the rear.
runners_data.comment: The Highway Rat is yet to win in his last five starts, though a second two starts back shows he can compete at this level. He has run over today's distance before and is quick to reappear, just six days on from his last start, with a string of sixth-place finishes elsewhere in that form the main concern.

runners_data.name: Sondad
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a visor; his good-ground record is thin (7/15 comparable runs), with wins coming on soft, and the fast conditions here represent a genuine concern for Joanna Mason's mount.
runners_data.comment: Sondad won two starts back, having been placed twice earlier in this sequence with a blank run in between, but managed only a below-par ninth last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a 28-day gap since that run adds a slight fitness question alongside the disappointing finish.

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: Five wins recorded at 6f on good ground in his recent history and a clean prominent style — this is exactly the race shape his profile is built for, and Jason Hart can slot him into the ideal second-rank berth.
runners_data.comment: Dark Thirty won last time out, and was also successful four starts back, landing two of his last six starts including a runner-up effort two starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a 21-day break, with the two blank runs elsewhere in that sequence the only blemish on a strong record.

runners_data.name: City House
runners_data.note: Prominent racer carrying a hood; form figures over 6f on good ground are consistent without being brilliant, and the step back from 7-8f recent runs back to this trip needs to translate quickly to be competitive here.
runners_data.comment: City House remains without a win in his last six starts, though a runner-up effort furthest back and a fourth last time out show he stays competitive in this company. He has run over today's trip and going before, but a 34-day absence since that last run leaves a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Headmaster
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle retains the ride for Lynam; last win came over 6f on good ground and he's progressive — the hood suits, and a second-rank position behind Keke is achievable with a clean break.
runners_data.comment: Headmaster was runner-up last time out, having won two starts back and again four starts back, landing two of his last five starts. He has run over today's trip and going before, though the below-par efforts sandwiched in that sequence and a 34-day absence since his latest run are the concerns.

runners_data.name: Dark Ace
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has won twice in 2024 but predominantly on standard-to-slow surfaces (1/3 runs on good-equivalent going); going fitness is a legitimate flag that tempers the promising recent form string.
runners_data.comment: Dark Ace won three and four starts back, but has since been passed over for the minor placings, finishing third in each of his last two starts. He has run over today's distance before and returns on a 20-day break, with the recent dip in form the main query.

runners_data.name: Sir Les Patterson
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (p); OR dropped to 92 but no win on comparable going in the dataset and connections' 14-day record is modest — needs everything to fall right from a prominent pitch to be involved.
runners_data.comment: Sir Les Patterson won furthest back in this sequence but has since found only a fourth at best, with blank efforts either side of that placing and a sixth last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before, though a 34-day gap since his last start adds a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Red Evolution
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner in form who will be squeezed for prominent berths in this 21-runner field — his best figures come over 5f on good, and stepping to 6½f while also being pushed wider than ideal by the field density are dual concerns.
runners_data.comment: Red Evolution won three starts back after finishing second four starts back, but has since managed only a fourth and then an unplaced effort last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a 20-day break, with that recent dip in form the main concern.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner who has won over 6-7f on good ground recently; the crowded prominent tier means he is unlikely to achieve his preferred position, and the headgear note (p) suggests he can be tricky when not travelling smoothly.
runners_data.comment: Glory To Be won last time out, and also six starts back, but a ninth and a seventh sit between those two victories. She has run over today's trip and going before and is fresh on a 10-day turnaround, though she rates only a modest chance in this field on our figures despite the latest win.

runners_data.name: Genesis
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who wears blinkers/hood combination; two wins on good ground at 5-6f and a quick back-up run 20 days ago — needs the pace scenario to develop in his favour over this extra half-furlong.
runners_data.comment: Genesis won last time out, and also furthest back in this sequence, though a blank run and a fourth place in between show the form has been up and down. He has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a 20-day break, but sits down among the outsiders on our figures despite that recent success.

runners_data.name: Moltophino
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing blinkers/hood; 13/15 comparable-going runs but the form line shows a horse that finds the first two difficult to peg back — needs a pressured gallop to make any late impact.
runners_data.comment: Moltophino is winless in his last five starts, with only a fourth furthest back standing out from a run of moderate finishes. He has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a 20-day break, but the lack of a big form figure anywhere in that sequence is a concern.

runners_data.name: Oro Blanco
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two at 6-7f on good ground and a rapidly progressive three-year-old for Harrington — a true prominent racer who will jostle for position early rather than settle in midfield; if he gets a clean run, the form franks him as a serious player.
runners_data.comment: Oro Blanco arrives on the back of two wins in his last four starts and has run over today's distance before. He sits down among the outsiders on our figures, though, and with his yard managing just one winner from its last twenty-five in the past fortnight, that cold spell is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing a hood; six-year-old with one win on comparable ground in 15 tries — consistent without threatening, and the race shape needs to unravel completely for him to be a factor.
runners_data.comment: Cuban Grey's only win in his last six starts came four starts back, and he has since managed only a seventh, a ninth and a fourth. He has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a 20-day break, but sits toward the bottom of this field on our figures on the strength of that mixed form.

runners_data.name: Gavoo
runners_data.note: Consistent front-half racer with a visor who has won on good ground; bumped to the midfield band by the prominent surplus in this field, meaning Andrew Slattery will need to push forward early to recover his horse's natural position — energy cost is real.
runners_data.comment: Gavoo won four starts back and was runner-up last time out, though a ninth and a fourth sit between those two form lines. He has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a 24-day break, with that inconsistency the main knock against him.

runners_data.name: Back Down Under
runners_data.note: A prominent racer by nature whose going figures (13/15 comparable runs) are strong but whose finishing positions rarely trouble the judge — genuinely unlikely to bridge the gap even if the race shape softens.
runners_data.comment: Back Down Under remains without a win in her last five starts, with a run of modest finishes including a ninth and a blank effort earlier in that sequence. She has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a 20-day break, and the lack of a standout form figure anywhere is the concern.

runners_data.name: Go Athletico
runners_data.note: Oldest horse in the field at eight; wears a hood, genuine hold-up type with a course win on good ground over 6f — needs the pace to collapse in the straight but has at least shown he can travel over the track.
runners_data.comment: Go Athletico is yet to win in his last six starts, with three blank efforts scattered through that sequence, but a runner-up finish last time out is a definite step up. He has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a 21-day break, though the string of blanks elsewhere makes him hard to fully trust.

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose recent form (including a placed effort over 6f on good) is solid; mapped slightly forward of his natural role — Denis Hogan's string is in excellent form (3/28 in 14 days) and Rory Cleary's course knowledge is an asset.
runners_data.comment: Alfred Tennyson is yet to win in his last six starts, though a runner-up effort three starts back shows he retains some ability. He has run over today's distance before and is quick to reappear, just seven days on from his latest sixth, but he sits down among the outsiders on our figures.

runners_data.name: Leveraging
runners_data.note: Long absence (211 days) is the dominant flag; natural prominent racer who has been displaced into midfield by the field's density — returning from seven months off into a 21-runner Good To Firm sprint is a very stiff ask.
runners_data.comment: Leveraging won last time out but that success came 211 days ago, with only a sixth and a ninth in the two starts before it. He has run over today's distance before, though he returns from a lengthy absence and sits bottom of this field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Keke is the confirmed front-runner here and, with a clear lead mandate on Good To Firm ground over 6½f at the Curragh, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable pace from the gates — this is not a field with a rival who will hunt Keke down from the off. The field does, however, contain a substantial cluster of genuine prominent-racing types — Oro Blanco, Red Evolution, Gavoo, Glory To Be, Back Down Under, and Leveraging — who will compete for the positions immediately behind Keke rather than settle into midfield as the pace map implies; the front of the race will be busier than a lone front-runner scenario might suggest, but the gallop is unlikely to become truly searching. On Good To Firm ground over this trip at the Curragh, a controlled pace set by one horse tends to produce a race that compresses in the final two furlongs, with prominent racers who travel smoothly just off the leader holding a decisive edge over genuine hold-up horses who will find insufficient room for a telling late challenge. This race shape firmly favours horses who can sit within two or three lengths of Keke in the first three furlongs and produce a clean, progressive run to the line — the hold-up brigade face a structural disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keke Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Keke leads at a measured gallop and the prominent horses behind travel smoothly into the straight.
scenarios.body: Keke sets a genuine but not punishing pace, and the chasers in the second rank — where several high-quality prominent types will actually settle — are poised to strike from two furlongs out; the Curragh straight rewards horses with class and tactical momentum over pure finishing speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Hotpot, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the battle among multiple prominent horses for position immediately behind Keke creates a stronger-than-expected gallop.
scenarios.body: The surplus of genuine front-running and prominent types forces a contested early pace that stretches the field and leaves the leaders vulnerable in the final furlong; hold-up horses with course form on this ground will be best placed to deliver late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Keke Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Keke bowls along at an uncontested honest clip that suits his front-running profile and the field finds the Curragh's flat six-and-a-half furlongs insufficient to reel him in.
scenarios.body: On Good To Firm ground with no serious early challenger, Keke can control tempo completely and build a lead that proves decisive; his recent course-and-distance form and trainer's sharp 14-day strike rate underpin a genuine front-running threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion of out-of-position prominent horses — Oro Blanco, Red Evolution, Gavoo — produces scrimmaging early that scrambles the anticipated race shape.
scenarios.body: Horses forced wider or unable to settle in their natural position lose ground and rhythm, and a runner who avoids trouble by tracking the right wheel throughout gains an enormous tactical edge; course-savvy jockeys with experience of the Curragh draw make the difference.

watchPoints.text: Oro Blanco, Glory To Be and Red Evolution will all attempt to press forward early in a 21-runner field — watch for a scrimmage in the first furlong that could tighten up horses on the inner and cause interference.

Keke's stamina over 6½f is genuinely unproven — if he ties up inside the final furlong after controlling the pace, the horse tracking him most cleanly (likely Dark Thirty or Bodhi Bear) will inherit the race.

Leveraging returns from 211 days off and is a prominent-style horse displaced into midfield — watch for an awkward early move as the jockey tries to find a position that suits, potentially hampering horses on his outside.

The Good To Firm going report is consistent across every race on the card — no softening expected, meaning any horse with a soft-ground dependency (Sondad in particular) should be treated with caution.

Adrian McGuinness saddles three runners (City House, Dark Ace, Go Athletico) — watch for any unexpected first-choice signal from his jockey booking, particularly on Dark Ace who has the freshest form among the three.

races.name: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Bucanero Fuerte
runners_data.note: Lightly raced over five and six furlongs this season with form figures of 37-754, De Aguiar's runner has the class to feature but arrives 56 days since his last run and is naturally a prominent racer who will struggle to secure his preferred position in this congested pace scenario; treat with caution until more recent evidence emerges.
runners_data.comment: Bucanero Fuerte is rated second of ten on our figures despite a lean recent sequence that has yet to produce a win, though fourth last time out was his best placing in his last four starts. Has raced over today's distance before, but a 56-day absence adds an obvious fitness question.

runners_data.name: Cover Up
runners_data.note: Crisford pair in good form (T14: 6/21) and James Doyle takes the ride on this six-year-old who has won twice on good going over five furlongs, most recently at this trip; shape suits him well as a genuine prominent type who won't need to fight for position, and 32 days between runs is fine.
runners_data.comment: Cover Up won twice in a row four and five starts back but has since faded, down to eighth and then unplaced last time out. Already has today's distance and going under his belt, and a strong speed figure keeps him in the midfield mix.

runners_data.name: Jakajaro
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's five-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner and Spencer will use that licence fully; his recent 1-1 at five furlongs on good ground is solid form, though the STYLE_FIT tag reminds us he is racing in a slightly unusual prominent role for this trainer/jockey combination and the pace he sets may ultimately serve others.
runners_data.comment: Jakajaro won two of his last five starts, backed by a strong speed figure and rated third of ten. He already has today's distance and going under his belt, and though his last two runs dipped to fourth and fifth, there's enough substance here to make him the pick.

runners_data.name: Kendall Roy
runners_data.note: McGivern's five-year-old has won twice at five furlongs on good ground and clearly handles the conditions, but has been mapped to a hold-up role purely because there is no room for another prominent horse — this is not where he wants to race, and the STYLE_FIT discount is real; his best chance requires a very hot pace and a clean late run.
runners_data.comment: Kendall Roy landed last time out but that followed two blank efforts, and he's only rated eighth of ten on our figures. He already has today's distance and going under his belt, though a modest speed figure is the main knock here.

runners_data.name: Partisan Hero
runners_data.note: Loughnane's six-year-old ran just 14 days ago and arrives very fit, with a recent third at five furlongs on good ground; naturally wants to race prominently but finds that slot unavailable in this field, so Keane will need to make the best of a compressed midfield position — STYLE_FIT flag applies.
runners_data.comment: Partisan Hero is rated bottom of ten here, though back-to-back thirds in his last two starts show current form is solid enough. A win three starts back is the standout, and he already has today's distance and going under him, but the moderate figures leave plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Rosy Affair
runners_data.note: Boughey's five-year-old has three wins from seven runs on good or good-to-soft going, is proven at five furlongs, and Billy Loughnane is a strong booking; with no redistribution flag, she is one of the few genuine prominent runners who should secure her natural pitch without a fight.
runners_data.comment: Rosy Affair boasts three wins in her last five starts, including a success two starts back, backed by a strong speed figure. Already has today's distance and going under her belt, with the only blot a fourth last time out, but she rates among the biggest dangers on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Brussels
runners_data.note: O'Brien's three-year-old has placed form at five furlongs on good ground but his last four runs read 2-4-6-0 and he arrives with a STYLE_FIT concern after being pushed back from his preferred prominent spot; Lordan will do what he can but this is an uncomfortable role and the recent form does not inspire.
runners_data.comment: Brussels was runner-up in two of his last five starts but the placings have since faded to sixth, fourth and unplaced. He already has today's distance and going under his belt, but he's yet to break through for a win in this spell.

runners_data.name: Charles Darwin
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore is a significant booking for the other O'Brien runner, and Charles Darwin's form of 1-1-8-0 includes wins on good going at five furlongs; naturally prominent but shown at hold-up due to redistribution — Moore's positional intelligence may help him navigate from a deeper slot better than most in this situation.
runners_data.comment: Charles Darwin won three in a row before his form dipped sharply, down to eighth and then unplaced in his last two starts. He already has today's distance and going under his belt, but the sudden decline leaves obvious questions with ratings only middling for this grade.

runners_data.name: Havana Anna
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's three-year-old won over six furlongs on good recently and has placed at five; Gavin Ryan rides and she arrives without a redistribution flag, making her one of the horses who should race in a natural prominent position — stamina through the final furlong of a flat five will be key.
runners_data.comment: Havana Anna sits top of our figures and boasts a win two starts back, though an unplaced effort three starts back and a below-par fourth last time out temper the picture. She already has today's distance and going under her belt, and remains a leading danger on quality alone.

runners_data.name: Ipanema Queen
runners_data.note: De Aguiar's second runner, a three-year-old with a win at five furlongs on standard going, is mapped to midfield as a redistributed prominent type; DBM is a gifted jockey who may make the most of whatever gap appears, but OR 93 is the lowest in the field and the redistribution away from a preferred prominent position is a real disadvantage in Group 2 company.
runners_data.comment: Ipanema Queen won five starts back and was runner-up next time, but the placings have since faded to seventh, fourth and sixth. Already has today's distance and going under her belt, and rated ninth of ten with a modest speed figure, she's hard to trust up in this company.

races.paceDynamic: Jakajaro is the confirmed pace-setter here and, with Jamie Spencer aboard, will be allowed to roll from the front and control tempo on good-to-firm ground over this straight five furlongs at the Curragh. The real story of this race shape, however, is that virtually every runner in the field carries prominent-racing tendencies — Bucanero Fuerte, Partisan Hero, Brussels, Rosy Affair, Cover Up, Havana Anna and Charles Darwin all want to race close to the pace, meaning the battle for early position behind Jakajaro will be fierce and contested rather than orderly. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can physically accommodate; Jakajaro is most likely to secure the lead, with Rosy Affair and Cover Up best placed to take up the immediate prominent slots given their tactical speed and cleaner recent form, while Brussels, Partisan Hero and Bucanero Fuerte are likely to find themselves racing further back than they would ideally choose. On a flat, straight track with a strong pace set by Jakajaro and multiple horses burning energy fighting for position in the early stages, the profile that benefits most is the horse who can race comfortably just off the early pace without over-exerting, then sustain their effort all the way to the line — a prominent-to-midfield horse with proven finishing speed on good-to-firm ground is ideally placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jakajaro Controls, Prominent Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Jakajaro sets a strong but sustainable gallop and the scrimmage for the prominent berths burns out the pace-pressers, leaving horses with a clean prominent pitch to close.
scenarios.body: Jakajaro dictates from the front on a flat track that suits a confirmed front-runner on good-to-firm, but the sustained scramble for position just behind drains those who fight hardest for it; the horse who slots into a comfortable prominent position without wasting early energy is delivered to the business end of the race in the best shape. Cover Up and Rosy Affair, both proven at five furlongs on good ground with recent winning form, are the profiles most likely to benefit from this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Blows Up, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the battle for prominent positions results in a genuinely hot early tempo that stretches the field and leaves the front group vulnerable to a late run from deeper.
scenarios.body: Horses pushed back from their natural prominent position — Charles Darwin, Kendall Roy — find themselves involuntarily racing from further back than ideal, but if pace is strong enough they could stay on powerfully in the final furlong of a straight track. This scenario is partially constrained because the true hold-up types are actually redistributed prominent runners, so their finishing kick may be less devastating than that of a genuine closer.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jakajaro Leads And Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Jakajaro is allowed a soft enough lead that he conserves energy and finds a finishing gear late, winning without being seriously pressured.
scenarios.body: Spencer is a master of conserving horses and the Curragh straight five suits a front-runner who can control fractions; if the prominent battle rages behind him and nobody has the pace to go with him early, Jakajaro could steal enough of a break that the field cannot reel him in. His STYLE_FIT flag indicates he is racing somewhat outside his typical profile but his recent form of 1-1-4-5 on similar ground keeps this live.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Splits Field, Flank Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the draw creates a physical divide in the race and a horse on an advantaged flank receives cleaner air and a straight run throughout.
scenarios.body: On a straight five at the Curragh, wide draws can allow a horse to avoid the congestion caused by a big field of prominent types all trying to settle close to the pace; a runner who draws wide and travels fluently without interference could emerge late with more energy intact than those caught in the scrimmage. This is the lowest-probability shape because the straight track at the Curragh tends to compress the field rather than create extreme draw bias, and no runner here is a true hold-up type who thrives on a lone wide run.

watchPoints.text: Jakajaro (front runner) is the pivot of this entire race — if Spencer opens up a clear lead in the first furlong unchallenged, the race may already be half-won; watch how quickly Cover Up and Rosy Affair move to track him.

The battle for the prominent positions behind Jakajaro in the first two furlongs will be intense given Bucanero Fuerte, Partisan Hero, Brussels, Cover Up and Rosy Affair all want to race close to the pace — any horse caught wide and forced to use early energy in that scramble will be at a significant disadvantage.

Charles Darwin is the most interesting of the redistributed horses because Ryan Moore rarely allows a positional problem to become a race problem — watch whether he angles for a gap on the rail or takes a wide berth to travel comfortably from a deeper pitch.
Kendall Roy's recent form (1-10-13 latest three) is volatile and his forced hold-up role makes his chance very scenario-dependent; only live if the pace genuinely burns out the prominent group.

Going is officially Good To Firm for this race (confirmed in the going report for the 3:25), which is faster than the header states as Good — horses with proven form on firmer ground such as Cover Up (two Good wins at 5f) hold an edge over those with a question mark at the sharp end of the going spectrum.

races.name: GAIN Railway Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: Consistent performer for O'Brien with two wins and three placed efforts in similar good ground, but a natural front-end operator who is unlikely to secure a prominent position behind Tribeca in this field; Lordan will have to manage traffic from further back than ideal, which tempers confidence despite solid recent form.
runners_data.comment: Carry The Flag returns to winning form, following up a success four starts back with another last time out, with a below-par ninth the outlier in between. Top of our figures and with today's distance and going already covered, he rates the one to beat on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Celeron
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner over C&D for O'Callaghan with Murphy aboard, and the combination of course-distance form and a legitimate prominent position available makes this one of the best-placed runners tactically; 31 days since last run is a mild query but trainer form over the past fortnight (2/18) is acceptable.
runners_data.comment: Celeron won two starts back but was unplaced last time out, on a thin body of recent form. Already has today's distance and going under his belt, but he's rated bottom of this field on a modest speed figure, leaving plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Confucius
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes a horse who wants to race near the pace, but with Carry The Flag and The Scallionator also pressing forward, Confucius may find itself squeezed further back than its form merits; the 1/6f on good last time is relevant, though the style-fit discount applies given the crowded prominent tier.
runners_data.comment: Confucius won three starts back and backed that up with a third last time out, sandwiching a blip of sixth in between. Rated second of seven with a solid speed figure, he already has today's distance and going under his belt and looms as the chief threat up top.

runners_data.name: Immortal Guard
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's runner has won over C&D and has three from three at the same distance on similar ground, which is solid form — however, this horse's natural pace preference means it arrives in a hold-up slot only by default rather than by design, so a late run from the rear would require the pace to be higher than expected.
runners_data.comment: Immortal Guard won three starts back and has stayed competitive since, third and then second in his last two starts. Already has today's distance and going under his belt, and rated third of seven, though a modest speed figure of 79 is the main knock against the leading pair.

runners_data.name: Switching Sides
runners_data.note: Harrington's filly beat Celeron on debut before finishing second behind the same rival, establishing a clear form link with one of the key market rivals; Shane Foley can slot into a genuine tracking position and the 36-day gap since last run is the primary query.
runners_data.comment: Switching Sides won last time out to follow a runner-up effort, a short but tidy recent record. Already has today's distance under his belt, though he's rated only sixth of seven on a modest speed figure, leaving him with plenty to find in this company.

runners_data.name: The Scallionator
runners_data.note: Mulvany's 90-rated runner has placed form in this grade over C&D and is genuinely keen to race forward, but being pushed into a midfield role by the weight of prominent types means Joyce will be navigating rather than dictating; the style-fit discount is real and limits expectations.
runners_data.comment: The Scallionator won two starts back after a runner-up effort three starts back, but the campaign has since stalled with an unplaced run last time out. Already has today's distance and going under his belt, and a moderate speed figure fits a mid-pack finish rather than a leading role.

runners_data.name: Tribeca
runners_data.note: Keane and De Aguiar's runner won over this C&D last time having finished well beaten over 5f on debut, and the step to 6f clearly suited; as the lone confirmed front-runner she has full control of the pace narrative, and the question is whether her class (OR 120) is sufficient to hold off two rivals on the same rating who will have a clear sight of her all the way up the straight.
runners_data.comment: Tribeca won two starts back but was unplaced last time out, a mixed recent picture. Already has today's distance and going under his belt, and rated fourth of seven, he has the figure to feature if that below-par run last time proves the outlier.

races.paceDynamic: Tribeca is the confirmed front-runner here and, with Colin Keane aboard, is almost certain to stride into an uncontested lead from the gates on this flat 6f Curragh track in good-to-firm conditions. The pace will be genuine but controlled — Tribeca sets it alone and is not going to be harried, meaning the tempo is unlikely to be ruinous for those racing prominently just behind. Celeron and Switching Sides, both rated 120 and with course-and-distance form, are best placed to track that lead from a true prominent position and pounce when Tribeca's advantage narrows in the final furlong. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers with the class to sit a length or two off a solo leader and produce a clean, straightforward finish — horses who can travel smoothly and deliver a sustained effort rather than a late sprint from deep. This field contains more genuinely prominent types than the race shape can accommodate at the front: Carry The Flag, Confucius, and The Scallionator are all natural front-end horses who are unlikely to secure their preferred position behind Tribeca, leaving Celeron and Switching Sides best-placed to exploit the prime tracking berths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tribeca Controls, Class Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Tribeca leads uncontested and Celeron or Switching Sides tracks cleanly before striking in the final 1.5f
scenarios.body: Tribeca sets a sustainable solo lead on good-to-firm ground, and the two OR-120 horses positioned just behind have the class and course-distance form to reel her in at the death; this shape suits horses who can travel smoothly off a genuine but not suicidal pace and produce a clean finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tribeca Goes Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Tribeca's early advantage proves too great for the trackers to close and she holds on strongly
scenarios.body: Keane dictates a pace that is just quick enough to stretch the field but not destructive for Tribeca herself, and if the challengers leave their run fractionally too late on fast ground the leader can be hard to peg back over 6f; this shape rewards a front-runner with a strong cruising speed and an honest finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of prominent types causes early crowding and fractional pace disruption that scrambles the anticipated race shape
scenarios.body: Carry The Flag, Confucius, and The Scallionator pushing forward creates pressure Tribeca did not expect, lifting the early pace and compressing the field into a more ragged shape through the first three furlongs; in this scenario a horse who finds a clean passage and can switch off before producing a late surge benefits, though true hold-up types are scarce and any late dash comes from horses who are not natural closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to set up a meaningful closing run from the back of the field
scenarios.body: Immortal Guard is the only horse mapped anywhere near a hold-up position, though it is a redistributed prominent type rather than a genuine closer, meaning a late-pounce outcome depends on conditions that are unlikely to materialise in a 7-runner race where the leader is expected to control tempo; the scenario carries low weight precisely because no true hold-up specialist is in this field.

watchPoints.text: Celeron and Switching Sides share identical OR (120) and near-identical C&D form — whichever secures the cleaner prominent position behind Tribeca through the first two furlongs is likely to dictate the finish.

Carry The Flag, Confucius, and The Scallionator are all natural front-end horses who cannot all get their preferred spot — watch the first 1f for crowding and jostling that could unsettle Tribeca's rhythm or impede a runner unexpectedly.

Tribeca's lone front-running role is a significant tactical asset, but Keane must judge the pace precisely on good-to-firm ground — if she is allowed to coast too slowly she will be a sitting target, and if she goes too fast she risks emptying before the line.

Immortal Guard's three runs have all been over this trip in similar going and all have produced a placed or winning finish — despite the redistribution to a hold-up role, Donagh O'Connor may try to push forward early and reclaim a more natural position if gaps allow.

races.name: Juddmonte Irish Oaks (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Amelia Earhart
runners_data.note: Solid form at 1m2f-1m4f on good ground with two wins from five similar-going starts, but her naturally front-running tendencies mean she is unlikely to get the pitch she wants in this traffic-heavy field — expect her to be squeezed back from her preferred position from the off.
runners_data.comment: Amelia Earhart won two in a row three and two starts back but stepped back to sixth last time out. Already has today's distance and going under her belt, but she's down at rank ten of eleven and a 43-day gap adds a fitness query, leaving plenty to prove at this level.

runners_data.name: Beautify
runners_data.note: Six runs on good ground without a win, but this 1m4f trip is unexplored territory for her and she is one of only two genuine hold-up horses in the race; trainer O'Brien knows the distance suits and she could creep into contention if the pace is strong enough to string the field out.
runners_data.comment: Beautify rates third of eleven and carries a strong speed figure despite modest recent finishes, a runner-up five starts back the best of them. Already has today's going under her belt, but remains without a win in that spell, with two runs of sixth most recently a concern.

runners_data.name: Cameo
runners_data.note: Won a 1m4f maiden at The Curragh on good ground and clearly stays the trip, but with her prominent style she is among several O'Brien runners competing for the same early positions — Chris Hayes may find himself settling for a deeper berth than planned.
runners_data.comment: Cameo won three starts back but the placings either side have been workmanlike, fifth, fifth and fourth among them, with a third her latest effort. Already has today's distance and going under her belt, and a fair speed figure keeps her firmly in this midfield mix rather than the leading group.

runners_data.name: Composing
runners_data.note: Moderate recent form — best finish a third — and her hood suggests some temperament management is needed; she wants to race prominently but is another who will be crowded out, and her overall level of ability makes it hard to see her winning even in an ideal scenario.
runners_data.comment: Composing rates second of eleven, well above what her recent fifths and sixths would suggest. She already has today's distance and going under her belt, and a third five starts back is the best of this run — but she's still without a win here.

runners_data.name: Earth Shot
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner with strong solid form — two wins and two seconds from four starts — including a 1m4f win on good ground; James Doyle is an astute jockey for a race like this and her prominent yet tractable style should allow her to find a clean position just off Thundering On.
runners_data.comment: Earth Shot won last time out to add to a win three starts back, an admirably consistent alternating sequence of wins and seconds. Already has today's distance and going under her belt, and rated fourth of eleven with a fair speed figure, she looks sure to go close again.

runners_data.name: Inis Mor
runners_data.note: Two wins from five starts on good ground and a proven 1m2f performer stepping up to 1m4f; Oisin Murphy is an excellent tactician for a compressed field and Inis Mor's prominent style is credible here given she has the physical class to slot into a forward position if others are shuffled back.
runners_data.comment: Inis Mor won two starts back but that followed an unplaced run and preceded a solid third last time out, a mixed recent picture overall. Has today's going under her belt, and a fair speed figure fits a mid-pack finish rather than a leading role in this field.

runners_data.name: Johanna Walsh
runners_data.note: Fitted with a tongue tie and drops in after a 1m4f second on good ground — the form profile points directly to this race; Colin Keane is the standout domestic jockey booking and she has the tactical versatility to sit just off the pace and challenge once Thundering On's advantage narrows.
runners_data.comment: Johanna Walsh won two starts back and was runner-up last time out, after a pair of thirds earlier in this sequence. Already has today's distance and going under her belt, and a fair speed figure fits a mid-pack finish rather than a leading role.

runners_data.name: Rebel Moon
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two starts — both on good ground at 1m2f — and clearly progressive, but she is a natural front-runner who will struggle to secure her preferred position with Thundering On in the race and several other prominent types filling the early slots; J M Sheridan faces a serious positional problem.
runners_data.comment: Rebel Moon has won both starts in this recent sequence, a perfect record on paper, but sits only ninth of eleven on our figures with a modest speed figure of 72. Stepping up against this quality asks a fresh question her form alone can't yet answer.

runners_data.name: Sparan Nua
runners_data.note: Perfect three-from-three record, all on good ground including a 1m4f win, and Jim Bolger's runners often improve sharply at this level; Declan McDonogh will need to manufacture a prominent position quickly because her natural style demands it, and failure to do so significantly blunts her winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Sparan Nua is unbeaten in three starts on paper, but sits bottom of our rankings with a modest speed figure of 79. Already has today's distance under her belt, though the perfect record alone doesn't square with such a low figure against this field.

runners_data.name: Sugar Island
runners_data.note: Wore a hood previously and has mixed form at 1m4f on soft, but her genuine hold-up profile is genuinely rare in this field — one of only two true closers — which gives Wayne Lordan licence to sit quietly and pounce late if the pace is sufficiently strong.
runners_data.comment: Sugar Island won three starts back but that followed a well-beaten ninth, and she's since added a fourth and a third to a mixed picture. Already has today's distance under her belt, and a fair speed figure fits a mid-pack finish, though a 43-day gap adds a query.

runners_data.name: Thundering On
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner at OR 119 and the only confirmed front-runner, so McMonagle has a free hand to dictate; won over 1m2f on soft and 1m4f on soft, and while Good to Firm is faster than ideal based on her best form, the positional advantage she holds in this shape is enormous.
runners_data.comment: Thundering On won back-to-back starts three and two starts back after two earlier runner-up efforts, and tops our figures with a strong speed figure to match. Already has today's distance and going under her belt, and though fourth last time out is a mild blot, she rates the one to beat.

races.paceDynamic: Thundering On is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eleven-runner Group 1, and with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, Dylan Browne McMonagle can control tempo from the front on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f at The Curragh. The pace is likely to be honest rather than scorching — a measured, sustainable gallop that keeps the race together until the tempo lifts in the straight, playing into the hands of horses with a strong finishing kick from just off the lead. This field contains a significant surplus of prominent-running types: Earth Shot, Inis Mor, Johanna Walsh, Cameo, Composing, Amelia Earhart, Rebel Moon and Sparan Nua all want to race prominently, meaning many will be shuffled back from their natural position and the tactical shape will be more compressed than the drawn positions suggest. Horses who can travel smoothly in behind the controlled pace and produce a sustained late run — genuine hold-up and midfield performers — are best placed, along with any prominent type fast enough to sit second or third and kick early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Kicker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Thundering On dictates an unchallenged, measured tempo that compresses the field and sets up a decisive finishing burst in the straight.
scenarios.body: Thundering On rolls along at an honest clip with no one brave enough to challenge her early, the field bunches behind her, and at the two-furlong pole the race becomes a sprint-finish test; horses with the highest cruising speed from a prominent position and the cleanest passage are best rewarded.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Thundering On sets only a modest pace and kicks early enough that the field cannot reel her in on fast ground.
scenarios.body: With Good to Firm conditions rewarding sustained galloping and Thundering On rated OR 119 — the highest in the field — McMonagle times his run to perfection, pressing the button from two furlongs out before closers can wind up; the premium-rated favourite simply outstays a compressed chasing pack.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent group creates early tactical jostling that briefly inflates the early fractions and flatters the genuine hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: Beautify and Sugar Island, both true hold-up types, are able to stalk the pace unobstructed and swoop late once the field's congestion in the middle stages blunts the kick of those who had to work hard to find position; the honest pace suits horses who can close off a strong gallop rather than those forced to race out of character.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Outsider Claims
scenarios.trigger: If the scramble for prominent positions among Amelia Earhart, Rebel Moon, Sparan Nua and Cameo produces a falsely run, stop-start race that scrambles form.
scenarios.body: Erratic fractions cause the race to be won by a horse that sneaks a soft lead or pounces through gaps at the top of the straight; Sparan Nua, unbeaten in three and very much at home on Good ground over the trip, could profit if she manages to grab a workable position before the bunch compresses.

watchPoints.text: Thundering On holds a structural monopoly on the front-running position — if McMonagle gets a soft lead and finds Good to Firm conditions more agreeable than her form figures suggest, she could be very hard to catch from the front.

Monitor the first two furlongs closely for Rebel Moon, Sparan Nua, Amelia Earhart and Cameo all attempting to assert prominent positions simultaneously — a messy early exchange could compromise multiple fancied runners' races before the field settles.

Earth Shot's jockey James Doyle is travelling from Britain for a key ride: watch whether she jumps cleanly and slots into second or third, as that position could be the most coveted piece of real estate in this race shape.

Beautify and Sugar Island are the only authentic hold-up types — if the pace is strong and the field strings out, their late challenges become disproportionately dangerous relative to their odds, as they will not be compromised by the prominent-runner overcrowding.

Going to Firm conditions across the card at The Curragh may favour horses who have previously shown their best on a sound surface — cross-reference each runner's historical going figures before the off, as the official Going listed as Good in the race header does not match the card-wide Good to Firm reports.

races.name: Hill Of Allen Stud Handicap

runners_data.name: Genchev
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with Colin Keane aboard for the ever-dangerous G M Lyons yard; holds solid form at 10-12f on good ground with a win and three placings in similar conditions, and an uncontested lead here is a significant tactical gift — though a style-fit flag tempers expectations of winning from this position in a strong-pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Genchev won two starts back and finished second three starts back, pointing to solid form ahead of a blank effort last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before and sits at the top of this field on our figures, with that below-par latest run the one blemish on an otherwise strong profile.

runners_data.name: Vanir
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this improving three-year-old who has run exclusively in good ground and won his last start at 12f, making him the most course-and-distance-relevant prominent runner; sits just a pound below the top weight and is ideally placed to capitalise on a controlled pace set by Genchev given his three-from-three record in similar going.
runners_data.comment: Vanir won last time out, having been runner-up the run before that - a marked improvement on the below-par eighth that preceded it. She has run over today's distance before and returns quickly on a 17-day turnaround, with just three recent runs to judge her on.

runners_data.name: Yousaynothingatall
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for Joseph Patrick O'Brien, a yard firing at 20/56 over the past fortnight; naturally wants to race prominently but is squeezed into a midfield map by weight of competition at the front — his two runs at 12f on good-ish ground produced a win and a placing, and his chance depends on recovering something close to his natural position early.
runners_data.comment: Yousaynothingatall has been a picture of consistency, placing in four of her last five starts including a win two starts back, and has run over today's distance before. Her yard is among the in-form stables of the moment too, landing over a third of its runners in the past fortnight, with a 44-day gap since her latest outing the only slight query.

runners_data.name: Noble Honour
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a mare who has placed in all three career starts, including twice at 10f on good ground, but like Yousaynothingatall she is a genuine prominent racer pushed rearward by the congested pace map — her chance is contingent on a stronger-than-expected gallop opening gaps in the straight, and her OR of 78 leaves room to improve if conditions unfold favourably.
runners_data.comment: Noble Honour is yet to win in her last three starts, but has been placed in all of them, including a runner-up effort last time out. She has run over today's distance before, though her yard has landed just one from its last twenty-five runners in the past fortnight, and a 43-day layoff adds to the concerns.

runners_data.name: Trustmore
runners_data.note: Entirely unknown running style (tagged U) for Oisin Murphy and Stephen Thorne; three runs all on good ground at 7-10f have yielded no wins or places, the headgear flag (b) suggests connections are still searching for the key, and until a clearer style profile emerges he is a difficult horse to map confidently onto any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Trustmore is winless in his last three starts, without threatening the places in any of them, and he has run over today's distance before. A 43-day absence since his last outing adds a further concern, leaving little in his recent form to recommend him.

runners_data.name: Tanzanite Diamond
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up runner in this field for Adam Caffrey and Adrian McGuinness; four career runs are all at 10-12f on good ground with a placing at 10f, and while the trip suits on paper, a late challenge is structurally disadvantaged here because Genchev's uncontested lead is likely to produce a pace insufficient to string the field and create the late gaps this horse needs.
runners_data.comment: Tanzanite Diamond is yet to win in his last four starts and sits bottom of this field on our figures. He has run over today's distance before, and while a third two starts back shows he can be competitive, a 36-day break since his last outing is a further concern.

races.paceDynamic: Genchev is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival for the lead in a field of six, he is set to coast into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at the Curragh. Vanir is the most likely companion in the prominent berth, with Yousaynothingatall and Noble Honour — both natural front-runners by inclination — pushed back into a midfield mapping because this field holds more prominent types than can realistically secure those positions simultaneously; Genchev and Vanir are most likely to actually occupy them. Tanzanite Diamond is the sole genuine hold-up runner, with Trustmore a complete unknown on style. The race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or just off a controlled, honest pace on fast ground — a tempo that is likely to be sufficient to stretch the field without inviting a late swoop, benefiting those settled in the first two or three positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Genchev Controls, Vanir Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Genchev sets a measured, uncontested gallop and the field strings out on the good-to-firm surface from the early stages.
scenarios.body: Genchev dictates from the front at a pace he controls entirely, softening rivals who try to close, while Vanir — settled just behind and boasting a win over course-and-distance in similar going — produces a clean challenge entering the straight with nothing left in the tank behind. This shape is the default read: one free leader, a solid prominent stalker, and fast ground that rewards horses who have been on the bridle throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just sharp enough to string the field but Genchev ties up late, allowing one of the crowded prominent group to assert.
scenarios.body: Yousaynothingatall or Noble Honour, unable to get their natural position early but tracking the pace from the third or fourth slot, hit the rising ground in the Curragh straight with momentum if the pace slightly quickens their passage. The fast ground suits horses who have been travelling economically and can produce a sustained rather than explosive finish — a profile that fits both displaced prominent types here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Picks Up Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If the front group sets a stronger-than-expected pace and Tanzanite Diamond is delivered late off a searching gallop.
scenarios.body: Tanzanite Diamond is the only genuine hold-up type in the field and benefits exclusively when the leaders have genuinely emptied themselves — a less likely outcome given Genchev's uncontested lead promises a controlled tempo. On fast ground over 1m2f at the Curragh the closing run is a long way to make up ground unless the early pace has been injudiciously fast, which the race shape does not encourage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Race Shape
scenarios.trigger: If there is unexpected pressure for the lead early, significantly lifting the early tempo and causing the field to bunch or spread unusually.
scenarios.body: A frantic early exchange would scramble positions and bring Trustmore, whose style is entirely unknown, into theoretical contention if he happens to be sitting ideally. Tanzanite Diamond could also benefit from a genuine end-to-end gallop, but the small field of six on an open Curragh straight makes sustained chaos structurally unlikely given the clear pace hierarchy.

watchPoints.text: Vanir is the most dangerous horse in the race if Genchev sets a comfortable tempo — watch whether Ben Coen positions him directly behind the leader from the off, as any gap to the front-runner will be the critical tactical moment entering the straight.

Yousaynothingatall and Noble Honour are both naturally prominent but cannot both get there — watch the first two furlongs to see which, if either, manages to slot behind Genchev rather than being pushed back into midfield, as position at the first bend will define their chances entirely.

Trustmore's unknown running style under Oisin Murphy is a structural wildcard — if he breaks sharply and contests the early lead, the pace dynamic changes immediately and all scenario probabilities shift; watch his early action out of the gates.

The going at the Curragh has been reported as Good to Firm all day, which is faster than the declared Good for this race — on ground this quick the Curragh straight can stretch fields quickly, and horses who are caught flat-footed at the top of the straight will find it very hard to close.

races.paceDynamic: Namiid is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner sprint, and with no genuine rival likely to press her hard for the lead on Good To Firm ground at the Curragh, she should be able to control tempo from the front without burning excessive energy — a sustainable, measured gallop rather than a frenetic dash. Behind her, Real Encounter, Final Melody, Sovereign Cry, Happy Henry and Nouvel Espoir will all look to track close to the pace in the prominent berths, creating a compressed, bunched shape through the early stages. With so many prominent types, those unable to secure their natural position early will be shuffled into unfamiliar mid-division roles, reducing their effectiveness — this is a race that shapes to favour horses who can sit just off the pace in the first three or four, travel smoothly, and produce a clean, direct finish without needing to weave through traffic. The field holds more prominent types than can all get their position; Namiid looks most likely to lead, with Real Encounter and Happy Henry best placed to lock in the prime tracking spots, while Carrigans Grove — a natural prominent runner — is pushed into midfield by the congestion. This pace shape tilts the advantage toward tractable, well-positioned prominent racers who get a clear run, as the moderate tempo will not be fast enough to string out the field and allow deep closers to arrive with momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Namiid sets a sustainable gallop and the prominent trackers travel smoothly into clear daylight from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Namiid dictates a steady tempo, allowing the horses immediately behind to conserve energy and pounce with a sustained run from the two-furlong pole; with the pace neither too fast nor too slow, those locked into the prime tracking positions have first run on the field. Prominent types who settle just behind the leader without fighting for position will find this tempo perfectly suited to their style.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Strong Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types push each other along faster than intended and the early pace overheats despite one nominal leader.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected tempo set by jostling prominent runners burns them off in the final furlong, opening a window for horses who have been dropped back slightly to finish powerfully through the weakening pack. Hold-up horses who genuinely get back — Focaccia and Daneh Of Dandy — are best equipped to exploit a fade from those who burned energy disputing position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays the Field
scenarios.trigger: If Namiid gets a completely uncontested lead and the gallop is slower than expected, allowing her to coast and sprint clear late.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied, Namiid settles into her own rhythm and finds a gear change in the final furlong that a strung-out, traffic-affected field cannot match; the Murtagh stable runner, who has already won over this course and distance on Good ground, is ideally set up for exactly this scenario. Prominent types who travel well in second will be nearest but may lack the acceleration to peg back a fresh, unextended leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a scramble with significant interference and redistributed hold-up types get a clear passage wide at a crucial moment.
scenarios.body: A messy race with crowded rail positions forces a wide split, and horses who find themselves in the uncongested outer — including some of the repositioned hold-up types — can sustain a run all the way to the line through tired rivals; this is the least likely shape given the field's true profile, as most redistributed closers are not genuine deep hold-up horses. Apache Outlaw's versatile profile gives him slight edge in this chaotic scenario over a largely out-of-role cohort.

watchPoints.text: Namiid's tempo is the race pivot — if Jessica Maye (7lb claim) sets a genuinely comfortable pace unchallenged, she controls the race; watch whether Real Encounter or Sovereign Cry attempt to push up and apply pressure in the first furlong.

Happy Henry's headgear and Good-ground course form make him a live runner, but Leigh Roche must secure a prominent position immediately from the gate in a field this large — any traffic trouble or slow break will be costly.

Nebrook Star's 175-day absence is the standout fitness flag in the field; Diego Lima will need this horse to come forward sharply from a cold start over a trip that offers no margin to find rhythm gradually.

Multiple redistributed hold-up horses — Harry's Hill, Mary Shoelaces, Imperial Dream, Absoluteassignment and Tawaazon — are mapped forward of their natural position; if any of these get stuck wide early searching for space, they will compromise their own chances further and could interfere with runners in the outer berths.

The Curragh 5f is running Good to Firm across every race on the card, confirmed by the going report — any horse with a going concern on fast ground (none flagged here, but check paddock sweat) should be noted pre-race as conditions are unlikely to ease.
